clue.text: Ample time to cut back after start of past year

indicators.note: after says the period of abstinence follows the opening letter of past
start of picks just the opening letter of the word past

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season when people give up treats

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a generous allowance of time to make savings once last year got under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time to cut back' looks like an instruction but is a cryptic description of the forty days before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a supply that is more than enough, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Liberal attitude over time needed for keeping stock

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the earlier letters on top of the word for time

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a Liberal in politics
an air is a manner or attitude someone puts on
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A permissive approach, given long enough, is what a stockman needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lairage is a holding pen where livestock rest, for instance before market or slaughter.

clue.text: Describing some hooter or some klaxon as 'a loudspeaker'

indicators.note: the second some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A description of car horns and loud klaxons, comparing them to public address systems.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'or' into the definition; 'or' is the link word, and the hidden-word signal is the second 'some'. 'Hooter' is slang for a nose, though the surface reads it as a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooter is slang for the nose, and the adjective for anything relating to the nose is this one.

clue.text: Desires unknown income

parts.note: y is one of the algebraic letters standing for an unknown quantity
earnings are money coming in, an income

explanation.surface: A wish for money from an unexpected source.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural nouns for longings or cravings, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Name for vase showing things the returning sailor craves

parts.note: a sailor coming home longs to reach port
a homeward sailor also longs for dry land

explanation.surface: A sailor home from sea dreams of a famous vase, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both pieces: the harbour and the solid ground a seafarer yearns for.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Roman cameo-glass vase in the British Museum is known by this name, after the Duchess who owned it.

clue.text: Soldier's correct tally — not all personal items?

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier
proper means correct or right

indicators.note: not tells us to remove the word all from tally

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier checks that his kit tally is right, yet some of it is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' looks like 'incomplete' but tells us to remove ALL from TALLY, leaving TY.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessions belonging to an individual rather than the public; the question mark admits the phrase usually means land or premises.

clue.text: Nitrogen found in most of region around the kidney

indicators.note: found in says the chemical symbol sits inside the shortened word
most of drops the last letter of the word for region

parts.note: a realm is a region or domain
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about nitrogen detected in tissue near the kidney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims REALM to REAL, and 'found in' places N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective used in medicine for anything relating to or located near the kidneys.

clue.text: What's very funny about duplication of state message?

indicators.note: about says the texting abbreviation wraps round the repeated state

parts.note: LOL, laugh out loud, is what you text when something is very funny

indicators.note: duplication of means the state's abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why it's hilarious when a state's message is repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: CAL is a recognised short form of California.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone conversation within the same area is a kind of communication, so the answer is an example of a message.

clue.text: Gas worried very young child

parts.note: neon is a noble gas
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: Gas pains have upset a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' takes the sense of something gnawing at you: ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for a newborn infant in its first weeks, so a very young child.

clue.text: Discouraging comments is unsaid, so goes wild

indicators.note: goes wild says the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone holds back negative remarks, and so loses control.
explanation.definitionFit: Words aimed at putting someone off a course of action are persuasion against it.

clue.text: Firm and sure to spoil

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
OK means sure, as in agreement

explanation.surface: A firm that is certain to go bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To falsify accounts, or in chess problems to ruin a composition with an unintended solution, is to spoil it.

clue.text: Newspaper's line encountering an old military leader

parts.note: a rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid's story about meeting a veteran general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encountering' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Raglan commanded British forces in the Crimean War, so he was a nineteenth-century army commander.

clue.text: Call out to gain knowledge of curtailed safety announcement

indicators.note: out signals that the word call is rearranged
curtailed cuts the tail, the last letter, off the word for study

parts.note: to learn is to gain knowledge of something

explanation.surface: An instruction to call out for information about a cut-short safety notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call out' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'out' rearranges CALL into ALLC; 'curtailed' cuts LEARN to LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal that danger has passed is a standard announcement that it is safe again.

clue.text: That agreement about musical selection's right, based on annual returns

indicators.note: about says the archaic word for that goes round the musical faculty

parts.note: yon is an archaic word for that
an ear is the faculty of discriminating musical sounds
yea is an old word of agreement

explanation.surface: A contract about choosing music is declared correct, judging by yearly figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is a container signal; 'That' is the archaic demonstrative, and 'musical selection' is the faculty of telling musical sounds apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures compared with the same period twelve months before are measured on this basis, from one annual result to the next.

clue.text: Rake gathering bally nuts in deep shade

indicators.note: gathering says the dissolute man holds the rearranged letters inside him

parts.note: a roué is a rake, a dissolute man

indicators.note: nuts signals the letters of bally are scrambled

explanation.surface: A libertine collects a pile of nuts in a dark corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the thing being gathered but turns BALLY into YALBL, which ROUE surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich, strong blue colour is a particular deep hue, so it is a shade.

clue.text: Practical article is reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are looked at again and reordered

explanation.surface: A useful newspaper piece is under review.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sensible and pragmatic, dealing with things as they are, is down to earth.

clue.text: A lot of noise obscuring first murder victim

indicators.note: obscuring first hides the opening letter of the word for a din

parts.note: a babel is a confused din of voices

explanation.surface: A racket drowns out the story of the very first murder victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' looks as if it belongs with the victim, but it tells us which letter BABEL loses.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Cain's brother is slain by him, the first person killed in the Bible.

clue.text: Looking old, when avoiding looking slimy

indicators.note: avoiding says the little word for when is left out of the longer word

parts.note: greasy means slick and slimy-looking
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone appears aged, but at least not oily.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair turning silver is a sign of age, so the colour word describes someone looking elderly.

clue.text: Jumper's back needing something scraped off? That's due to bird

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: needing something scraped off removes the final letter from the word for back

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: The back of a sweater needs a stain scraped off, the result of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a sweater but is a kangaroo; STERN loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel, the male domestic fowl, is a kind of farmyard bird.

clue.text: Smooth cryptic Listener holding mother back

indicators.note: holding says the rearranged letters wrap round the reversed parent
cryptic suggests the letters are disguised by reordering
back says the word for mother is turned round

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A puzzle-solving reader of a cryptic magazine smooths things over with their mum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard British crossword series, so 'cryptic' reads as its description, not as an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something more efficient or sleek by removing excess is to smooth it, as a verb.

clue.text: Royal partner about to be announced in sport

indicators.note: about says the royal mistress's name goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A royal's companion is about to be revealed in a sporting role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be announced' reads as a verb phrase but is the abbreviation TBA. Nell Gwyn was an orange-seller turned actress and royal mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A team game where players score by throwing a ball through a high hoop, an example of a sport.

clue.text: Medicine in water knocked back? Here's possible reward

indicators.note: knocked back, like a drink downed, says the whole assembly is turned round
in places the tablet inside the body of water

parts.note: a pool is a body of water
a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: A dose of medicine swallowed with water, then a treat for being brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests drinking the medicine but reverses POPILLOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet on a stick is a classic treat given to a child as a prize for good behaviour.

clue.text: Indicate one's name engraved in trophy

indicators.note: engraved in says the letters are cut into the cup

parts.note: a pot is slang for a sporting cup or trophy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Showing where someone's name is etched on a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: To show the direction of something with a finger is to indicate it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Prompt opening of newspaper after one's getting mention

indicators.note: after says the newspaper's first letter follows the numeral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: opening of takes just the first letter of newspaper

parts.note: to cite is to mention or quote

explanation.surface: Someone is spurred by a front-page mention of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone to act is to urge or provoke them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Frustrate or frustrated?

explanation.surface: A puzzled query whether the word is a verb or an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means thwart; as an adjective it means annoyed.

clue.text: Endearment putting of Prince (and everyone else)

indicators.note: putting off (as printed, 'of') says the letter for prince is shed

parts.note: petal is an affectionate term of address

explanation.surface: A pet name dropped by a prince and his entourage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting of' should read 'putting off': PETAL sheds P.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation used in citations means 'and others', for the rest of a list.

clue.text: Amount allocated in rail working is not sensible

indicators.note: in places the allowance inside the rearranged letters
working suggests the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: a ration is a fixed amount allocated

explanation.surface: A quota allotted to railway operations is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges RAIL into IRAL, which holds RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illogical or unreasonable lacks good sense, so it is not sensible.

clue.text: Work includes arrangement of rites? Such work does

definitions.text: Work includes arrangement of rites? Such work does

indicators.note: includes says the word for work holds the shuffled letters

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it

indicators.note: arrangement of signals the letters of rites are reordered

explanation.surface: A question about whether a job involves organising ceremonies, answered yes for a cleric's job.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the work of a cleric does include arranging rites.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties characteristic of a member of the clergy, who conducts church ceremonies, are described by this adjective.

clue.text: Fort? Actors exited bypassing fort

parts.note: the cast is the body of actors in a production

indicators.note: bypassing says the abbreviation is skipped, removed from the word

parts.note: left means exited, went out

explanation.surface: Actors leave a fortress by walking round another fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified stronghold, such as a medieval keep, is a kind of fort, hence the question mark.
